_comment: Every threshold context-diet compares against lives here. The first run prints the effective table once, so a wrong default is visible before it misfires. Delete any key to fall back to the built-in default.

claude-opus-5.source: reported by the runner itself: claude -p --output-format json returns modelUsage[<model>].contextWindow, read 2026-09-19

claude-opus-4-8.source: peak single-prompt context observed in this machine's transcripts, measured 2026-09-19 with the iterations-aware numerator: 999,231 (not runner-confirmed; weaker evidence than the rows the runner reports)

claude-fable-5-1.source: not reported by the runner: claude -p --model claude-fable-5-1 returns an api_error, so no modelUsage. Kept at the same tier as claude-fable-5, corroborated by a peak single-prompt context of 933,273 in this machine's transcripts. Weaker evidence than the rows above.

claude-fable-5.source: reported by the runner itself: claude -p --output-format json returns modelUsage[<model>].contextWindow, read 2026-09-19 (the alias `fable` resolves to this canonical id)

claude-sonnet-5.source: lower bound only, not a documented window: peak single-prompt context observed in this machine's transcripts, measured 2026-09-19 with the iterations-aware numerator: 615,688. Listed at the observed floor rather than rounded up, because a window guessed too large is the failure that makes the monitor never fire. (not runner-confirmed)

claude-haiku-4-5-20251001.source: reported by the runner itself: claude -p --output-format json returns modelUsage[<model>].contextWindow, read 2026-09-19

_context_windows_note: These are the models' own ceilings, not the compaction trigger. settings.autoCompactWindow is taken first when it is set (spec order, Ben's decision of 2026-10-04), so with it at 500,000 every model here, Haiku included, is measured against 500,000. This table is used when the setting is absent, and a reading names the table window whenever it is smaller, which is the Haiku case: Amber at 250,000 is past the end of a 200,000-token session. A model that is absent from both still pauses monitoring and says so. One historical auto-compaction reads 1,316,455 and is deliberately not used as evidence of a larger window, because a multi-iteration record inflates that number by up to 2.00x.
_cold_turn_note: A turn whose cache_creation exceeds its cache_read, above this many prefix tokens, re-processed the conversation at the write price instead of reading it back. Below the floor a turn is too small to say either way. Checked against 413 transcripts on this machine: 4.5% of ordinary turns above 20,000 tokens cross this test, against 86% of the turns immediately following a compaction.
_timing_gate_note: Timing gates judge wall-clock, the time a user waits, against unchanged limits. Above this 1-minute load per core the machine is oversubscribed and wall-clock measures other programs: on 4 Oct the unchanged hooks read 55 ms at normal load and 248-307 ms at load 37-50 on 10 cores. The runner waits up to timing_gate_quiet_wait_s for load to fall, then marks the gate blocked by load, which is never a pass and makes the run exit non-zero.
_h2_growth_share_note: H2 is SUPPORTED when at least this share of sessions grew more than their turn-1 prefix, REFUTED at or below one minus it, and INCONCLUSIVE between. 0.6 was the literal in context_census.py before it became a key.
_mlflow_note: MLflow 3.16 put the filesystem tracking store into maintenance mode, so the default is a local SQLite file. It still needs no server and makes no network call. Set MLFLOW_ALLOW_FILE_STORE=true to go back to a file store.
